# Splitter

A resizable split between two panes: drag the handle, or focus it and use the keyboard.

**Interaction**: hovering the handle adds the shared state layer and shows a grip; dragging follows the pointer
(also when it leaves the handle) and keeps the pressed state. `Tab` focuses the handle and shows the focus
ring; `←` / `→` (`↑` / `↓` when vertical) resize by `step`, four times as much with `Shift`; `Home` collapses
the primary pane to `min`, `End` expands it to `max`, and `Enter` toggles between collapsed and the previous
size. Screen readers read the handle as a separator with its current size (`aria-valuenow`).

**Category**: Patterns · **Common uses**: A resizable sidebar or list next to details, editors with a preview, a resizable bottom panel

## Import

```ts
import { Splitter } from 'vellum-ui'
```

## Basic usage

A resizable list next to the details: drag the handle, or focus it with `Tab` and use `←` / `→`, `Home` and
`End`. The Splitter fills its parent, so the parent needs a height.

```tsx
import { Box, ListItem, Splitter, Stack, Text } from 'vellum-ui'
import { DemoFrame } from './_frame.tsx'

export function Basic() {
  return (
    <DemoFrame>
      <Splitter defaultSize={220} min={160} max={360} aria-label="Resize the file list">
        <Box surface="canvas" padding={2} grow>
          <Stack gap={1}>
            <ListItem title="Brief.pdf" selected onClick={() => {}} />
            <ListItem title="Moodboard.png" onClick={() => {}} />
            <ListItem title="Budget.xlsx" onClick={() => {}} />
          </Stack>
        </Box>
        <Stack padding={4}>
          <Text weight="semibold">Brief.pdf</Text>
          <Text tone="secondary">Updated 2 hours ago by Alex Kim</Text>
        </Stack>
      </Splitter>
    </DemoFrame>
  )
}
```

`DemoFrame` is only a fixed-height container of the examples; in a page, put the component in `Page fill` or `Panel fill`.

## Variants

### Vertical

`direction="vertical"` stacks the panes; with `primary="end"` the size belongs to the bottom panel, and the
top pane takes the rest.

```tsx
import { Box, Splitter, Stack, Text } from 'vellum-ui'
import { DemoFrame } from './_frame.tsx'

export function Vertical() {
  return (
    <DemoFrame>
      <Splitter direction="vertical" primary="end" defaultSize={120} min={64}>
        <Stack padding={4}>
          <Text>Editor</Text>
        </Stack>
        <Box surface="sunken" padding={3} grow>
          <Text mono size="xs">
            Build finished in 1.2 s
          </Text>
        </Box>
      </Splitter>
    </DemoFrame>
  )
}
```

`DemoFrame` is only a fixed-height container of the examples; in a page, put the component in `Page fill` or `Panel fill`.

## Advanced

### Remembered size

With `storageKey`, the size is saved on this device and restored on the next visit. `onSizeChange` reports
every change.

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react'
import { Box, Splitter, Stack, Text } from 'vellum-ui'
import { DemoFrame } from './_frame.tsx'

export function Remembered() {
  const [size, setSize] = useState<number | null>(null)
  return (
    <DemoFrame>
      <Splitter storageKey="examples.splitter" defaultSize={240} min={120} onSizeChange={setSize}>
        <Box surface="canvas" padding={4} grow>
          <Text tone="secondary">Sidebar</Text>
        </Box>
        <Stack padding={4}>
          <Text numeric>{size === null ? 'Drag the handle' : `${size} px`}</Text>
        </Stack>
      </Splitter>
    </DemoFrame>
  )
}
```

`DemoFrame` is only a fixed-height container of the examples; in a page, put the component in `Page fill` or `Panel fill`.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default | Required |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | `readonly [ReactNode, ReactNode]` | The two panes, in order. Each pane scrolls on its own when its content overflows. | — | Yes |
| `direction` | `'horizontal' \| 'vertical'` | `horizontal`: panes side by side with a vertical handle; `vertical`: panes stacked with a horizontal handle. The Splitter fills its parent, so give the parent a height. | `'horizontal'` | No |
| `primary` | `'start' \| 'end'` | The pane whose size is set (`size`, `min`, `max`); the other pane takes the remaining space. | `'start'` | No |
| `size` | `number` | Size of the primary pane in pixels (controlled); use it with `onSizeChange`. | — | No |
| `defaultSize` | `number` | Initial size of the primary pane in pixels (uncontrolled). | `280` | No |
| `onSizeChange` | `(size: number) => void` | Called with the new size while dragging and after each keyboard step. | — | No |
| `min` | `number` | Smallest size of the primary pane in pixels; `Home` collapses the pane to it. | `0` | No |
| `max` | `number` | Largest size of the primary pane in pixels; `End` expands the pane to it. Never larger than the Splitter itself. | — | No |
| `step` | `number` | Pixels per arrow key press; with `Shift`, four times as much. | `16` | No |
| `storageKey` | `string` | Saves the size on this device (in `localStorage` under this key) and restores it on the next visit. Use a key that is unique in your application, such as `'files.sidebar'`. | — | No |
| `aria-label` | `string` | Accessible name of the handle, "Resize" by default (follows `locale`); name what it resizes, such as "Resize the sidebar". | — | No |

Also accepts `testId` (rendered as `data-testid`), `aria-label`, `role` and `id`, like all primitives.

Does not accept `style` or `className`: appearance is adjusted only through the semantic props above and the theme.
